APPLICATION 07 / SURVEY

Bridge Pier & Port Underwater Inspection

Inspect below the waterline. Report what you find.

Inspect submerged bridge piers, quay walls, piles and jetties with a compact ROV, using camera and sonar to record scour, damage and marine growth.

Home / Applications / Bridge pier, port & marine structure inspection

Who this is for

Bridge owners, port authorities, marine contractors and inspection consultancies.

Project inputs

  • Structure list, drawings and inspection objectives
  • Water depth, current, tide and visibility
  • Launch location and vessel availability
  • Report format and position references required
Build a project brief

The short answer

Bridge pier and port structure inspection with an ROV records scour, concrete damage, corrosion and marine growth below the waterline without diving. A compact ROV such as the R-30 can be launched from a quay or small boat; add imaging sonar for turbid water, and plan the work around current and tide.

01

Define the structures and features

List the piers, piles, quay walls or fenders to inspect and the features that matter: scour around foundations, spalling, exposed reinforcement, corrosion, impact damage and marine growth.

02

Plan for current and tide

Rivers and harbours often have strong, changing current. Check the vehicle’s ability to hold position with the planned payload and tether, and schedule inspection around slack water where possible.

03

Use sonar where the water is turbid

Bridge and port water is often turbid. Imaging sonar helps locate structures and scour holes when the camera cannot, and gives context to close-up video where visibility allows.

04

Deploy from shore, deck or boat

Compact ROVs such as the R-30 can be launched by a small crew from a quay or small boat. Confirm the launch point, tether route and space for the control station.

05

Deliver a usable inspection record

Agree how each observation is tied to a structure, elevation and position, and the report format required by the owner. Request sample footage and a sample report.

BEFORE YOU SPECIFY

Frequently asked questions.

Can an ROV inspect bridge scour?

An ROV with imaging sonar can help locate and record scour around piers in turbid water. Measurement accuracy depends on the sonar type and reference method; agree the required output first.

Is the R-30 suitable for saltwater?

Confirm the supplied configuration’s suitability for seawater use, including materials, maintenance and rinsing procedures, in the quotation.
